The Specialty Outpatient Staff Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based specialty care to patients with oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants as appropriate to clinic setting.

Duties include but are not limited to: Patient care, care coordination, health promotion, health education and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management Assists in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic, specialty care through collaborative strategies with others.

Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence.

Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals Contributes professional nursing perspect in discussions with the interdisciplinary team Leads the integration of evidence-based practice/research with clinical expertise to improve quality of care and resource utilization with improved outcomes for the immediate practice setting Expands knowledge base and practice evaluation through mentoring, precepting, and/or teaching VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Full-Time, Monday-Friday, Day shift Compressed/Flexible: This position is not eligible.

Telework: This position is not eligible. Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Financial Disclosure Report: Not required. Notifications: This position is an AFGE Bargaining Unit position. Selectee may be required to work at any VA Connecticut Healthcare System campus, as needed.

Duties are but not limited to: Demonstrate proficiency in practice based on conscious and deliberate planning. Self-directed in goal setting for managing complex client situations. Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care.

Follows procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. The Mental Health (MH) Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to patients.

They will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and enhance outcomes utilization. The psychiatric MH RN independently provides patient-centered and recovery-oriented care and maintains self-awareness while caring for patients living with MH conditions.

They facilitate warm hand-offs, telemental health care, and nurse-led psychoeducational groups; use therapeutic communication techniques, practice de-escalation techniques, utilize recovery-oriented language, and provide Veterans, their family members, and/or significant others with education regarding their illness, medications, and treatment plan.

The MH RN actively participates in care coordination, liaising with Inpatient MH Units to facilitate continuity of care, MH interdisciplinary treatment team huddles and meetings and responds to psychiatric and medical emergencies as directed.

The MH RN reports and addresses safety concerns, document nursing triage assessments, risk screens, clinical reminders, and patient plan of care, according to facility policy. The MH RN maintains professional boundaries to protect patient vulnerabilities and act in the best interest of the patient.

The MH RN demonstrates competence in practice and decision-making, deliberate planning, and critical thinking skills. Promotes patient scheduling activities to maximize availability and workload capture. Provides accurate and timely documentation.

Who May Apply: U.S. Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education requirements described below.

OR A Bachelor's degree in a programs other than nursing is acceptable only if possession of a current, active, full, and unrestricted nurse license or registration as a professional nurse from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States is presented.

The incumbent of this position must have a valid, state-issued driver's license. The Registered Nurse (RN) - Mental Health Intensive Case Management - Psychosocial Rehabilitation and Recovery Center (MHICM-PRRC) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to patients.

The person in this role will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and enhance outcomes utilization.

The MHICM-PRRC program provides clinical community-based case management services to Veterans with serious mental illness (SMI), severe functional impairment, and high Inpatient MH unit utilization, in coordination with existing community and Veterans Affairs (VA) services.

The RN - MHICM-PRRC is also responsible for the following duties: Providing outpatient, community-based MH services for a subgroup of Veterans with PMI; including but not limited to transportation, medication management, in home/community consultation. Responding to psychiatric and medical emergencies, as directed.

Documenting nursing triage assessments, risk screens, clinical reminders, and patient plan of care in accordance with facility policy. Maintaining professional boundaries to protect patient vulnerabilities and act in the best interest of the patient. Collaborating and supporting MH nursing, along with other disciplines.

Demonstrating the ability to cope with and manage competing priorities, demonstrating proficient practice and decision-making, deliberate planning, and critical thinking skills. Holding therapeutic groups at the VA, outings in the community, treatment plans and meets with Veterans one to one to develop goals. Other duties, as assigned.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: Up 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Full-time (1 FTE); Variables (0800 - 1630, 0730 - 1600, or 0700 - 1530), based on the needs of the unit.

Physical Requirements: This position includes a level of physicality normally associated with duties performed by nurses such as direct patient care, and potentially long periods of walking, standing, sitting, moderate lifting, repeated bending, or kneeling.

Examples may include but are not limited to: Significant amounts of time standing assisting assigned patients Utilization of safe patient handling and mobility protocols Position specific duties/expectations are detailed in the associated competency and should be performed once the competency has been validated.

Other Significant Information: The MHICM-PRRC RN is expected to travel in the community/drive to see Veterans in their home, traveling in and dealing with all kinds of weather elements at various times. This position requires operation of a government-owned or leased motor vehicle to properly carryout assigned duties.

A valid, state-issued driver's license is required, along with medical clearance by Employee Occupational Health (EOH). The incumbent of this position would be considered an Incidental Driver.

Incidental operators are employees, other than those occupying a position officially classified as a motor vehicle operator, who are required to operate a government-owned/leased motor vehicle to properly carry out their assigned duties. This position potentially requires flexibility in schedule and assignments.

Duties include but not limited too: The GI clinic staff also travels to the ER, OR, or ICU to perform cases (including for on-call emergency cases). The Liver Clinic supports Veterans with different forms of Hepatitis, Cirrhosis, Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Drug Induced liver injuries to name a few.

Monitoring and sedating patients for GI Procedures and guided by the Moderate Sedation policy MCM 558-01-5.8 (pre, intra and post procedure). Assisting physicians with the technical aspects of endoscopic procedures within the endoscopy unit and during on-call or travel cases.

Preparing patients scheduled for endoscopic or biopsy procedures Monitoring the technicians and other support personnel related to safe patient care.

Education for patients and families related to pre-and post-procedures and medications, including diet and medication regimens Communicating with patients by telephone triage, secure messaging, or Annie App (text application) Participating in conferences and awareness events for GI and Liver cancers.

The Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA) IV administers anesthesia in both inpatient and outpatient settings for patients across all levels of health complexity. This role includes direct patient care, administrative duties, education, and participation in research activities.

CRNAs practice to the full extent of their education, training, and certification, with core functions defined by their clinical privileges or scope of practice. These privileges are established locally in alignment with state licensure requirements and Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) bylaws.

The CRNA IV provides advanced clinical practice, consultation, and management to support safe, high-quality anesthesia care. Duties include but not limited to the following: Collaborates with a variety of health care professionals to achieve common goals for care, safety, and welfare of patients.

Fosters high levels of confidence and satisfaction among patients and staff, as well as meet and exceed compliance standards.

Provides anesthetic services within five general categories to include: pre-anesthesia evaluation and preparation; anesthesia induction, maintenance, and emergence; post anesthesia care; peri-anesthetic and clinical support functions; and emergency response techniques.

Develops and implements a comprehensive anesthesia plan of care for patients requiring local, regional, general, and monitored anesthesia both inside and outside the Operating Room (OR) suite.

Ensures anesthetic services delivered throughout the facility are of the highest quality to promote patient safety, satisfaction, and improve outcomes and efficiencies. Functions as resource for staff education and is willing to be a preceptor and adjunct clinical faculty for health care trainees rotating through the facility.

Develops and implements evidence-based practices that are essential to the delivery of the highest quality anesthesia care. Prescribe appropriate preoperative, intra-operative and postoperative orders and medications.

Makes recommendations that may significantly affect the content, interpretation or development of VA policies or programs concerning critical matters or major issues within the anesthesia arena.

Coordinates education within the anesthesia department to include, but not limited to Phase I (non-clinical) and/or Phase II (clinical) for nurse anesthesia students or health care trainees who rotate through the VAMC. Provides ongoing education for employed CRNAs and other training activities within the department.

Responsibility for preceptor training and orientation. Administrative and technical responsibilities for maintaining professional standards of practice in accordance with the Council on Accreditation (COA) of Nurse Anesthesia Education Programs.

Develops and reviews orientation programs, journal club, scheduling, counseling, and grading, monitoring cases, mentoring research and/or formal scholarly projects, preparing and teaching lectures, providing hands-on lab/simulation instruction, administrative support, coordinating with didactic instructors, and clinical anesthesia.

Assists and provides development opportunities for primary clinical instructors and other department members to maintain their skills and keep current with progressive technical knowledge. Demonstrates a commitment to in-service training for staff and facility continuing education to provide accurate information to the population served.

Exemplifies the ICARE core values of-Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and Excellence. VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards This position is eligible for the Education Debt Reduction Program (EDRP), a student loan payment reimbursement program.

You must meet specific eligibility requirements per VHA policy and submit your EDRP application within four months of appointment. The Telemedicine Clinic Coordinator manages all aspects of a multi-disciplinary telemedicine program across multiple federal correctional facilities. Telemedicine coordination is performed within the scope of practice of a Registered Nurse (RN) as defined by licensing agencies and the BOP (current licensure must be maintained).

Facilitates telemedicine video visits between the inmate and the clinical provider via approved video teleconference communications (VTC). Establish strong relationships with outside hospitals and clinicians to transition the delivery of high-quality patient care from community-based to telemedicine-based care when appropriate.

Along with all other correctional institution employees, incumbent is charged with responsibility for maintaining security of the institution. The staff correctional responsibilities precede all others required by this position and are performed on a regular and recurring basis.
To be considered for the position, you must meet the following qualification requirements. Basic Requirements: Education: A graduate or higher level degree, bachelor's degree, associate degree, or diploma from an accredited professional nursing educational program is required.

This education must have been accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education, Council on Accreditation of Nurse Anesthesia Educational Programs, Accreditation Commission for Midwifery Education or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education at the time the degree was obtained.

Degree from Foreign Nursing School: Official certification from the Commission of Graduates of Foreign Nursing Schools is required for individuals who graduated from foreign nursing schools. AND Licensure: Applicants must have passed the National Council Licensure Examination.

In addition, they must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration as a professional nurse from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

Please electronically upload these documents along with your required supporting documentation at the time you apply.

The Registered Nurse- Maternity Care Coordinator (MCC) follows procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client care.

The Maternity Care Coordination is approximately 40% of the position with 60% PACT Outpatient Staff Nurse in Primary Care . Major duties and responsibilities of the position: Execute position responsibilities that demonstrate expert leadership, experience, and creative approaches in providing complex patient management.

Ensure the effective coordination of care between Veterans Affairs (VA) and maternity care providers in the community, and all relevant VA and community specialist providers treating the pregnant Veteran. Work with the local VA Medical Center (VAMC) Office of Integrated Veteran Care (IVC) to collaborate on referrals for care in the community.

Ensure coordination of care among relevant VA providers and the Women Veterans Program Manager (WVPM) and Women's Health Medical Director. Facilitates coordination of maternity care for pregnant Veterans on inpatient psychiatric units and/or in residential care programs. Monitor the provision of services and tracking of maternal and fetal outcomes.

Retrieve statistical data on maternity care and utilization at the local VAMC using Veterans Health Administration (VHA) databases. Ensure bimonthly telephone contact while the Veteran is in the care of the VA authorized provider in the community and documents the call(s) in the electronic health record (EHR).

Inform the Veteran of VA's authority to furnish newborn care and the need for other non-VA payment options (e.g., Medicaid) to be in place to cover any newborn care required beyond VA's authorization. Educate the Veteran on local and community resources (e.g., Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) Program).

Ensure the Veteran schedules postpartum care with the VA-authorized provider in the community. Provide the Veteran with information about the VAMC's process to obtain maternity care and health supplies (e.g., breast pumps, maternity belts, disposable nursing pads, breast milk storage bags, lanolin cream, intra-uterine devices).

Ensure that Veterans with positive screening results for depression, Intimate Partner Violence (IPV)/Domestic Violence (DV), Military Sexual Trauma (MST), and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) during their pregnancies or postpartum are referred to the appropriate specialists.

Evaluate care and outcomes to ensure timely and appropriate provision of services. Advocate for holistic care through Veteran/family education and provider interaction and implements an educational plan to meet the Veteran care needs. Collaborate in the development, implementation, evaluation, and revision of policies, procedures, and/or guidelines.

Demonstrate performance and leadership that is broad enough to improve the care for a group of patients. Provide peers with formal or informal constructive feedback for improvement. Support colleagues and other nurses through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care.

Foster a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of health care professionals. Evaluate outcomes of evidence based decisions and practice changes for individuals, groups, and populations.

Responsible for the documenting broad and complex outcomes at the program or service level, that can be demonstrated at any organizational level within a facility.

Duties and responsibilities of the Geriatrics and Extended Care Supervisory Assistant Nurse Manager include, but are not limited to: Geriatrics and Extended Care Supervisory Assistant Nurse Manager (ANM) supports the Nurse Manager (NM) in overseeing operations of a nursing unit/patient care area.

This role combines clinical proficiency with leadership responsibilities and is often considered part of the succession plan for future NM positions, providing opportunities to develop management skills and prepare for higher-level leadership.

Responsible and accountable for the direction and oversight of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance.

Exercises the authority to direct work, assign duties, evaluate employee performance, recommend employee awards, approve or deny leave, recall employees to duty, propose discipline, and to adjust their grievances, or to effectively recommend such proposed discipline or grievance adjustments for employees under their direct supervision, Serving as hiring official during the recruitment process for employees under their direct supervision of NM.

Applying clinical knowledge/judgment to lead staff involvement in planning, decision­ making, and evaluating outcomes; providing feedback to the NM who ultimately ensures nursing personnel provide timely nursing care that complies with generally accepted standards of practice Engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

Adheres to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. Promotes a workplace positively to achieve the organization's vision and mission.

They provide leadership in their assigned unit(s), including the Community Living Center (CLC), Inpatient and Outpatient Hospice/Palliative Care, Home Based Primary Care, and others as they are developed.

Responsible for participating within unit based and/or organizational level Shared Governance councils, utilizing clinical expertise, evidence-based practice, and knowledge to assist with finding solutions to problems or issues to improve the quality care provided to our veterans.

The Infection Preventionist (IP) Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based infection control practices. The IP establishes surveillance indicators and conducts monitoring to identify and reduce the risk of acquiring and transmitting infections among patients, employees, visitors, and students.

Contributes to the annual Infection Control Risk Assessment, determining appropriate resources needed to accomplish the proposed plan, communicating any variance to administration and revises plan as needed. The IP provides education on infection control issues, as well as annual and ongoing trainings to staff.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. The IP serves as an education resource for all employees on infection control, epidemiology, and provides knowledge and guidance.

Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing, while questioning clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based practices, to provide safe, quality nursing care. Collaborates with Employee Occupational Health (EOH) and other members of the interdisciplinary team to plan and implement the Immunization Program, i.e., influenza.

The IP assists the Infection Control Provider in managing the Clinical Case Registry (CCR) for Human Immunodeficiency Virus/Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (HIV/AIDS) and Hepatitis C, including providing reports and alerts to clinicians.

The IP has an important role in various programs and systems within the organization, i.e., Reusable Medical Equipment (RME), Construction and Water Safety committees. The IP participates in risk assessments for all construction projects and completes random walk-throughs of construction projects to inspect/review practices.

The IP implements and maintains a system for analyzing, trending, and reporting data. The IP assists in developing and maintaining mandatory documents such as standards operating procedures, policies, outbreak and exposure investigations, and external agency required documents.

The ANM acts as a supervisor, providing oversight for administrative tasks such as leave management, counseling, disciplinary actions, training, and evaluation of designated unit staff. The ANM applies necessary skills and coordinates or identifies educational and training needs for professional staff development and emerging needs at all levels.

Additionally, the ANM assists in creating a positive and supportive work environment to enhance care delivery and professional development for clinically competent staff. Major duties include but are not limited to: Responsible for contributing to the establishment and implementation of evidence-based best practices in nursing care.

Promotes professional governance initiatives and encourages participation of all staff. Serves as Acting Nurse Manager in the absence of the Nurse Manager. Serves as an assistant with authority delegated by the Nurse Manager, providing leadership, supervision, and direction to nursing staff.

Performs delegated duties including developing schedules, completing performance evaluations, and initiating or recommending disciplinary actions. Responsible for performance improvement, customer service, patient satisfaction, employee safety, and adherence to standards of care and practice, as well as accreditation and regulatory standards.

Collaborates with the Nurse Manager to assure responsibility and accountability for day-to-day clinical operations and patient flow, including supervision and evaluation of care delivered by all levels of nursing staff.

Identifies developmental and training needs of staff and provides support for such development and training per VA Handbook 500 Part 8. Conducts effective staff conferences and accepts responsibility for meetings, conferences, unit activities, direction, and follow-up with decided plans to improve patient care.

Leads or delegates group activities to solve problems or accomplish specific tasks, serving as a role model in comprehensive patient and family care and resolution of issues. Facilitates operational exchange of ideas between peers, managers, and staff, creatively responds to and evaluates suggestions for improvement.

Neben dieser täglichen sinnstiftenden Tätigkeit für den Patienten und die Gesellschaft bieten wir unseren Mitarbeitenden noch vieles mehr:
Ferien
Abschalten vom intensiven Arbeitsalltag - Ihre körperliche und geistige Erholung ist wichtig. Unser Arbeitszeitmodell ist so aufgebaut, dass alle Mitarbeitenden über das Jahr eine Woche Arbeitszeit vorarbeiten. Von diesem Vorholen der Arbeitszeit profitieren Sie mit bis zu einer Woche zusätzlicher Ferientage (Kompensationstage).
Wie alt sind Sie? Der Ferienanspruch ist bei uns altersabhängig. Mitarbeitende bis 49 Jahre profitieren mit diesem Arbeitszeitmodell von 6 Wochen Ferien pro Jahr, Mitarbeitende von 50 bis 59 Jahre von 6.5 Wochen und Mitarbeitende ab 60 Jahre von 7 Wochen.

Sie sind ein aktiver, geselliger Mensch? Unser Freizeitclub PDGR-AKTIV, der allen Mitarbeitenden offen steht, organisiert vielseitige Aktivitäten - ob Besuche im Bündner Kunstmuseum, Paintball-Wettkämpfe oder das Erklimmen verschiedener bekannter Bündner Berge - es hat für jeden etwas dabei. Haben Sie eigene Vorschläge? Bringen Sie diese ein oder organisieren Sie direkt selber einen Anlass.
Verwaltung bewegt
Profitieren Sie vom umfangreichen, gesundheitsfördernden Sport-Angebot der Kantonalen Verwaltung. Yogakurse, Nordic Walking, Gruppensportarten - stöbern Sie im attraktiven Programm von «Verwaltung bewegt».
Fitnessräume
Trainieren während sieben Tagen in der Woche? Die modern eingerichteten Fitnessräume in den Kliniken Beverin und Waldhaus nutzen Sie kostenfrei.
Minigolfanlage Beverin
Unsere Minigolfanlage liegt mitten in der ruhigen Umgebung der Klinik Beverin. Spielen Sie mit Freunden, der Familie oder mit Ihrem Team zu einem vergünstigten Preis.
Gesundes Essen
Unsere Küchencrews an den Standorten Beverin, Rothenbrunnen, Therapiehaus Fürstenwald und Waldhaus bieten Ihnen abwechslungsreiche und gesunde Mahlzeiten - zu einem vergünstigten Preis. Wir wünschen Ihnen «a Guata»!
Apfel- und Birnenaktion
Traditionsgemäss sorgt unsere 3-wöchige Apfel- und Birnenaktion im Herbst für eine energiereiche Zwischenverpflegung.
E-Bikes
Sie haben einen Termin in der Stadt? Nutzen Sie die PDGR E-Bikes für eine umweltfreundliche und nachhaltige An- und Rückreise.
Theaterverein Muntanellas
Sie spielen gerne Theater? Der PDGR-nahe Theaterverein Muntanellas bietet Ihnen die Möglichkeit, kreativ zu sein, in andere Rollen zu schlüpfen, Geschichten zu erzählen und der Leidenschaft fürs Theaterspiel nachzugehen.
13. Monatslohn
Selbstverständlich? Längst nicht alle Unternehmungen bieten einen 13. Monatslohn an. Bei uns ist die Auszahlung des 13. Monatslohnes selbstverständlich.
Besondere Sozialzulagen
Unseren Mitarbeitenden mit Kindern bieten wir, neben der Kinderzulage, besondere Sozialzulagen an. Die besondere Sozialzulage wird pro Familie ausgerichtet und ist abhängig vom Beschäftigungsumfang.
Berufliche Vorsorge
Unsere Mitarbeitenden profitieren von einer hervorragenden beruflichen Vorsorge mit attraktiven Leistungen der PKGR. Die PDGR leisten dabei einen überdurchschnittlichen Arbeitgeberbeitrag, der die gesetzliche Vorgabe deutlich übersteigt, was Ihre finanzielle Zukunft zusätzlich stärkt.
Beiträge an Kinderbetreuung
Berufstätige Eltern sind uns wichtig. Damit Sie Job und Familie optimal aufeinander abstimmen können, beteiligen wir uns an den Kosten für die Kinderbetreuung.
Zulagen
Arbeiten Sie nachts oder an Sonn- und Feiertagen? Diese Einsätze werden Ihnen finanziell entschädigt.
Leistungsprämien
Erbringen Sie ausserordentliche Leistungen oder haben Sie sich im hohen Masse engagiert? Dieser besondere Einsatz kann mit einer Leistungsprämie belohnt werden.
Spontanprämien

Unbezahlter Urlaub
Wollen Sie eine Auszeit nehmen? Wir geben unser Bestes, um Ihren unbezahlten Urlaub zu ermöglichen. Die Beantragung ist schnell und unkompliziert.
Externe Fort- und Weiterbildungen

### Ihre Stelle als Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH in Köniz auf einen Blick
**Position:** Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH

### Ihre Aufgaben als Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH im Tagdienst in Köniz
· Verantwortung für den gesamten Pflegeprozess von der Bedarfserhebung bis zur Auswertung
· Zudem: Durchführung ärztlicher Verordnungen sowie sichere Vorbereitung und Abgabe der Medikamente
· Überwachung von Vitalzeichen und frühzeitiges Erkennen von Zustandsveränderungen
· Fachliche Anleitung von FaGe, Pflegeassistenz und Lernenden im Team
· Ausserdem lückenlose Pflegedokumentation im elektronischen Pflegesystem
· Zusammenarbeit mit Ärzteschaft, Therapien und Angehörigen auf Augenhöhe
· Darüber hinaus Mitgestaltung von Pflegekonzepten sowie wir verbessern die Qualität stetig im Team
· Teilnahme an interprofessionellen Rapporten und Visiten im geregelten Tagdienst
### Diese Qualifikationen bringen Sie mit
· Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF oder FH
· Bei ausländischem Diplom: SRK-Anerkennung zwingend erforderlich
· Zudem Erfahrung in der Langzeitpflege, Akutpflege oder Reha
· Vor allem hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein, Empathie und Belastbarkeit
· Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (mind. Niveau B2)
### Ihr Arbeitsumfeld: Tagdienst im Pflegeheim
Diese Stelle ist im Tagdienst angelegt. Sie arbeiten also in einer klaren Tagesstruktur mit geregelten Übergaben am Morgen und am Abend. Dabei nehmen Sie an Rapporten im Team mit Ärzten und Therapien teil, koordinieren Termine mit Ärzten und Therapeuten und begleiten Angehörigengespräche. Somit verbinden Sie fachliche Verantwortung mit einem planbaren Alltag.
Kurz gesagt: Als Pflegefachfrau oder Pflegefachmann HF/FH im Tagdienst verbinden Sie fachliche Tiefe mit einem Alltag, der Planung zulässt. Genau deshalb ist die Stelle als Pflegefachfrau HF/FH im Tagdienst in Köniz bei Berufsleuten mit Familie so beliebt.
### Der Beruf im Detail: Was macht eine diplomierte Pflegefachperson HF/FH?
Diplomierte Pflegefachpersonen HF/FH tragen die fachliche Verantwortung im gesamten Pflegeprozess. Sie erheben zum Beispiel den Pflegebedarf, planen anschliessend die Massnahmen, führen sie durch und werten die Ergebnisse aus. Zudem steuern sie die Medikamentenabgabe, überwachen Vitalzeichen und erkennen Veränderungen im Gesundheitszustand frühzeitig. Damit sichern sie Tag für Tag die Qualität der Pflege.
Der Weg in diesen Beruf führt über die dreijährige höhere Fachschule (HF) oder das Bachelorstudium in Pflege an einer Fachhochschule (FH). Beide Abschlüsse berechtigen zur eigenverantwortlichen Berufsausübung.

Ausländische Diplome benötigen dafür eine [Anerkennung durch das Schweizerische Rote Kreuz (SRK)](https://www.redcross.ch/de/srk-anerkennung). Ausserdem stehen erfahrenen Fachpersonen attraktive Weiterbildungen offen, etwa ein Nachdiplomstudium (NDS), die Funktion als Berufsbildnerin oder die Teamleitung.
Der Arbeitsmarkt für Diplomierten Pflegefachpersonen in der Region Köniz ist durch hohe Nachfrage geprägt, insbesondere im Tagdienst. Sie profitieren von zahlreichen Stellenangeboten in Spitälern, Kliniken und Pflegeeinrichtungen.

Envie de nous rejoindre ? Alors, nice to meet you !
Infirmier\-conseil ou Infirmière\-conseil expérimenté\-e en psychiatrie et en soins à domicile
En tant qu’infirmier·ère\-conseil, tu rejoins une petite équipe engagée, dont la mission est de s’assurer que les prestations de soins infirmiers réalisées au domicile comme en EMS répondent aux exigences de qualité de soin et respectent le cadre légal en vigueur.
Ce que tu fais au quotidien
Au cœur de l’activité, le contrôle des mandats médicaux, des évaluations de soins requis et de la facturation des soins en psychiatrie et en somatique à domicile te permet de contribuer activement à la qualité et à la conformité des prestations fournies aux assurés. Tu veilles également au respect des dispositions légales et conventionnelles par les fournisseurs de soins.
Tu assures la gestion de dossiers de soins infirmiers complexes. À partir des documents transmis par les fournisseurs ou lors d’évaluations au domicile, tu évalues et analyses les besoins en soins des assurés et établis et rédiges les garanties de prise en charge octroyées.

Infirmier en santé mental
Description de l'entreprise
Pour notre partenaire, une clinique de jour spécialisée dans la prise en soins de patients présentant une crise psychique ne nécessitant pas de traitement hospitalier, nous recherchons un\-e infirmier\-ère pour un poste fixe.
La mission de la clinique de jour est d'offrir une prise en charge intensive sur une période de 5 à 6 semaines, à plein temps, du lundi au vendredi. L'objectif est de favoriser la stabilisation psychique des patients et de les accompagner vers un suivi durable et adapté à leurs besoins.
Les patients bénéficient de l'accompagnement d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire composée notamment de médecins, psychologues, infirmiers, assistants sociaux, art\-thérapeutes et aides\-soignants.
Poste à 100% du lundi au vendredi de 08H à 17h30
Description du poste
Accueillir et prendre en charge les urgences psychiatriques.
Assurer des soins subaigus de courte durée.
Participer aux consultations psychiatriques, psychothérapeutiques et psychologiques ambulatoires.
Réaliser des prestations de soins : entretiens, bilans sanguins, ECG et accompagnement à la médication.
Participer aux interventions dans le milieu de vie des patients lorsque nécessaire.
Contribuer à l'animation et au suivi des groupes psychothérapeutiques.
Collaborer aux prises en charge complémentaires telles que l'art\-thérapie et l'ergothérapie.
Participer au bilan et au suivi social en collaboration avec les professionnels concernés.
Assurer des entretiens de suivi dans le cadre d'obligations de soins émises par les autorités.
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe pluridisciplinaire afin d'assurer une prise en charge cohérente et de qualité.
Profil recherché

## L'entreprise : HUG ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour consulter notre rétrospective 2025 en cliquant ici.
Le Département de médecine de premier recours (DMPR) a pour mission sociétale de permettre un accès aux soins de qualité pour tous par une médecine de proximité, d'assurer la prise en charge des urgences médicales et chirurgicales légères, de promouvoir la prévention auprès des citoyennes et citoyens, d'apporter les connaissances médicales aux investigations judiciaires et de promouvoir la santé des voyageurs et voyageuses.
Le service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire assure la prise en charge de patients ayant voyagé et présentant une pathologie d'importation, tropicale ou parasitaire et prodigue des conseils de prévention. Il effectue des vaccinations spécialisées pour les voyageurs, les expatriés, les étudiants et la population locale. Par ailleurs, ce service participe activement aux interventions vaccinales en cas d'épidémie ou autre besoin identifié.

## Description du poste ##
En qualité d'infirmier ou infirmière au Service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire (SMTH), votre mission consiste à mener de manière autonome des consultations infirmières de pré-voyage auprès d'une patientèle très diversifiée (expatriés, familles, humanitaires, immunosupprimés).
Vous menez et gérez des consultations infirmières de première ligne de manière autonome, dans le respect des missions, des protocoles et des délégations qui vous sont confiés.
Vous assurez également une activité de conseil aux voyageurs et voyageuses en formulant des recommandations personnalisées en matière de prévention des risques liés au voyage (vaccinations, prophylaxie, mesures d'hygiène, prévention des maladies infectieuses et autres risques sanitaires). Vous participez activement aux campagnes de vaccinations sur différents sites.
Vous travaillez en collaboration avec une équipe pluriprofessionnelle ainsi qu'avec les réseaux de soins internes et externes, notamment les organisations non gouvernementales, les organisations internationales et les partenaires présents au Global Health Campus.
Votre empathie, votre sens du relationnel et votre capacité à créer un climat de confiance vous permettent de vous positionner comme un partenaire de soins à part entière.
Doté ou dotée d'une excellente capacité d'adaptation et de l'organisation, vous êtes en mesure de faire face à des flux de patients importants et variables tout en maintenant une prise en charge de qualité. Vous gérez sereinement les imprévus et les situations génératrices de stress.
Vous possédez d'excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens développé d l'accueil et une communication bienveillante, vous permettant de répondre aux attentes d'une patientèle exigeante et multiculturelle.
Dans le cadre de votre activité, vous êtes amené ou amenée à intervenir sur deux sites.

Une formation en médecine tropicale et des voyageurs constitue un réel atout.
Vous disposez d'un très bon niveau d'anglais, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit. La maitrise d'une autre langue, constitue un atout.
Vous savez vous adapter à divers contextes, aux imprévus, aux variations de charge de travail.

The Nursing Perioperative Service is seeking a dedicated Registered Nurse with a minimum of three years of Operating Room (OR) experience. The ideal candidate will demonstrate proficiency in circulating and scrubbing for a wide range of surgical procedures, ensuring adherence to aseptic technique, patient safety, and infection control protocols.

Must hold an active Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) certifications prior to appointment. Duties include but are not limited to: Preoperative assessment, intraoperative patient monitoring, safe and timely administration of medications, and diligent documentation of surgical procedures and patient outcomes.

Collaborate closely with surgeons, anesthesiologists, and support staff, actively participate in time-outs and safety checks, and provide patient and family education regarding perioperative care.

Additional duties encompass inventory management, participation in quality improvement initiatives, compliance with national and VA standards, and ongoing staff education and training. A strong commitment to Veteran-centric care and support for the mission of the Veterans Health Administration are essential.

Expected to function proficiently in both the circulator and scrub role within the OR and to be competent in all surgical specialties served. Maintains knowledge of current Association of peri-Operative Registered Nurses (AORN) standards, Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Directives, and service level standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Assures the sterility of the surgical field is maintained and all instrumentation and equipment in play is used in a safe and efficient manner.

Protects the patient from injury caused by chemical, electrical, mechanical, and thermal sources, and extraneous objects, performs counting procedures to protect the patient from unintended retained surgical items, participates in the Time Out process to ensure correct site, side, and level, and follows implant and tissue/tissue-based product documentation, policy, and procedures.

Manages the patient's specimens in the appropriate manner, administers medications safely and correctly, performs interventions to maintain the patient's wound and tissue perfusion at or above baseline levels, and performs interventions to protect the patient from surgical site infection.

Ensuring comprehensive documentation of all care provided during the perioperative experience is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record. Responsible for knowing what reusable instruments, equipment, medical devices, or supplies are in use in the clinical area.

Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour découvrir les moments forts et chiffres clefs de l'année 2025 en cliquant ici.
Comptant près de 1'200 collaboratrices et collaborateurs, le Département de médecine aiguë (D-MA) inclut les Services d'anesthésiologie, de pharmacologie et toxicologie cliniques, des soins intensifs et des urgences.

Il répond à une quadruple mission au travers de ses services qui apportent leur expertise en interaction fréquente avec l'ensemble des Hôpitaux universitaires de Genève, grâce à un plateau transversal, dans l'objectif d'assurer la meilleure prise en charge possible des patients et patientes.
Le Service d'anesthésiologie est un service transversal des HUG au cœur du plateau technique. Avec ses 8 unités médicales et une unité de recherche et d'innovation, sa mission vise à assurer le confort et la sécurité des patientes et patients au cours d'actes thérapeutiques ou diagnostiques, médicaux ou chirurgicaux, ainsi que lors des soins post-interventionnels, tout en veillant à la bonne prise en charge de la douleur.

## Description du poste ##
Vous assurez la prise en soins globale des patients et patientes, durant leur séjour dans les unités de soins péri-interventionnelles du Service d'anesthésie en collaboration avec les intervenants et intervenantes internes et externes.
Vous accueillez, accompagnez et prodiguez des soins à une patientèle nécessitant une surveillance continue, monitorée dans différentes salles de surveillances post-interventionnelles, avec une intensification du traitement dans une unité de soins intermédiaires péri-interventionnelle.
Vous promouvez et développez les soins infirmiers au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire.
Vous garantissez la sécurité du patient et de la patiente et réalisez des prestations de qualité dans un environnement de soins aigus.
Votre périmètre de travail peut inclure d'autres unités d'Anesthésiologie (Accueil ambulatoire, Antalgie interventionnelle, etc.).
## Description du profil ##
Vous êtes en possession d'un Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers ou d'un diplôme en soins infirmiers reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous avez travaillé dans un service de soins aigus ou suivi une formation certifiante (Certificat en soins intermédiaires).
Vous possédez des compétences confirmées dans la pratique des soins. Une expérience en soins aigus est indispensable.
Vous faites preuve de disponibilité et de ponctualité. Vous êtes apte à promouvoir la qualité des soins et à travailler tant de manière autonome que dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire.
Vous possédez d'excellentes capacités d'analyse, de synthèse, d'organisation, de gestion des priorités et de résistance au stress.
Vous êtes une personne ouverte aux changements et à la remise en question de vos pratiques.
Vous avez de l'aisance dans les relations humaines et possédez une forte capacité d'écoute et d'empathie.
Vous vous engagez à suivre une formation certifiante (Certificat en soins intermédiaires).

· Abschluss als Expertin oder Experte Anästhesiepflege NDS
· Erfahrung im OP oder im Akutbereich, sodass du sicher bist
· Selbstständig arbeiten und im Team helfen, damit alles gut läuft
· Ruhig bleiben, auch wenn es stressig wird, sodass du den Überblick behältst
· Klar sprechen, damit alle dich verstehen und gut zusammenarbeiten
### Das erwartet dich
Du findest eine Stelle, die dir Sicherheit gibt und dich weiterbringt, sodass du dich entwickeln kannst.
· Offene Stellen:[https://www.med-ipersonal.ch/offene-stellen](https://www.med-ipersonal.ch/offene-stellen)
· Direkt bewerben:[https://www.med-ipersonal.ch/jetzt-bewerben](https://www.med-ipersonal.ch/jetzt-bewerben)
· Unterstützung durch unser Temporärbüro Pflege Hünenberg, damit du schnell starten kannst
· Unterstützung durch unser Personalbüro für Pflege in Hünenberg, damit du dich wohlfühlst
· Weiterbildung, sodass du dein Wissen ausbauen kannst
· Ein Team, das dich unterstützt, damit du sicher arbeiten kannst
